title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (the 'situation clef' of p.137). Y is a smooth analytic space, in practice a multiplicity space or orbifold such as the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}. Θ is a normal crossings divisor on Y; for M_{g,ν} it is the boundary. Θ^{(d)} denotes the codimension-d skeleton (the d-fold self-intersection locus) and Θ^{(d)*} its open stratum. D'' → D' → Y are local immersions of smooth spaces factoring through skeleta of Θ, with D'' the deeper stratum. The transcription's codimension bookkeeping on p.137 is garbled, but the structure is clear: D'' sits in D' ∖ D'*. For each such D there is a 'multinormal principal bundle' P_D. This is the (C*)^d-torsor of frames of the d line-bundle summands of the normal bundle, one summand per local branch of Θ. Equivalently, up to homotopy, it is the deleted tubular neighbourhood of D in Y∖Θ. P_{D*} is its restriction to the open stratum D*. Its fundamental group π_1 P_{D*} is the 'local fundamental group at infinity' along the stratum. For M_{g,ν} it is the stabiliser in the Teichmüller modular group of the corresponding multicurve, with branches labelled. It is a central-type extension of the orbifold π_1 of the stratum (a product of smaller moduli spaces) by Z^d, the Dehn twists.

This page introduces three maps.
- (231) A canonical 'generalisation' morphism γ_{D'',D'} : π_1 P_{D''*} → π_1 P_{D'*}, from the tube group of the deeper stratum to that of the shallower one. It is defined up to the usual base-point ambiguity. Geometrically, points of the punctured tube of D'' that lie near the D'-branches but away from the extra branches are points of the punctured tube of D'*. For mapping class groups this is the inclusion Stab(σ'' ⊃ σ') ⊂ Stab(σ') of multicurve stabilisers.
- (232) The trivial map π_1 P_{D'*} → π_1 P_{D'}, induced by the inclusion P_{D'*} = P_{D'}|D'* ↪ P_{D'}.
- (233) The composite of (231) and (232), which must be π_1 P_{D''*} → π_1 P_{D'}. Grothendieck remarks that this composite is 'essentially trivial', because there is an evident morphism of bundles between P_{D''} and P_{D'}. Restricting the D''-frame to the branches belonging to D' gives P_{D''} → P_{D'}|D'' → P_{D'}.

The next page states the expected commutative square (234): i_{D'} ∘ γ = (π_1 P_{D''} → π_1 P_{D'}) ∘ i_{D''}. It stresses that γ itself comes from no map P_{D''*} → P_{D'*}, since the image of D'' lies in D' ∖ D'*. It then begins the construction of γ via a tubular-neighbourhood germ.

Purpose: to organise the tube groups of all boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν} into a functorial system, a 'structure à l'infini'. This is the Lego/Teichmüller-tower picture of the Esquisse, with generalisation maps between strata as structure maps.
errors: (233) as transcribed (π_1 P_{D'*} → π_1 P_{D'}) duplicates (232). The composite of (231) and (232) must have source π_1 P_{D''*}; either the manuscript omits a prime or the transcription misreads it.

The 'evident morphism' is read as P_{D'} → P_{D''}, but the natural map (restricting frames to the D'-branches) goes P_{D''} → P_{D'}. This is the direction used in the bottom row of (234) on the next page, so it is a slip of the pen or a misreading.
The codimension conventions on p.137 (which of D'', D' has codimension d_0 or d_1, and d = d_1 − d_0) are garbled in the transcription. On this page only the order matters: D'' is deeper than D'.

ideas.what: Multinormal principal bundle P_D (frames of the branch-wise normal line bundles) as a model of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a normal-crossings stratum; π_1 P_{D*} as the local fundamental group at infinity
ideas.modern_name: Punctured normal bundle / tangential base points along boundary strata; inertia–decomposition groups at infinity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura; Nakamura; later Hoshi–Mochizuki, Boggi in the profinite setting
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the structure at infinity of the M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower, without this formalism

ideas.what: Canonical 'generalisation' morphism γ_{D'',D'} from the tube group of a deeper stratum to that of a shallower one, not induced by any map of spaces
ideas.modern_name: Generalisation (exit-path) maps; functor from the exit-path category of a stratified space to groups; inclusions of multicurve stabilisers in mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson; Treumann; Lurie (exit-path ∞-categories). For moduli of curves: Harer, Ivanov; the Lego picture of Grothendieck's Esquisse, developed by Nakamura, Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, Lego), only informally

ideas.what: Compatibility square (234) relating γ to the trivial maps induced by P_{D*} ⊂ P_D and P_{D''} → P_{D'}
ideas.modern_name: Naturality of specialisation/generalisation maps in the stratified homotopy type

missed.claim: The generalisation maps γ between punctured-tube fundamental groups of the strata of a normal crossings compactification amount to a functor on the exit-path category of the stratified space (Y, Θ). Grothendieck sets this up explicitly, with base-point subtleties and compatibility squares, for M̄_{g,ν}, well before exit-path categories were formalised. It connects his 'structure à l'infini' with later stratified homotopy theory.
missed.quote: un morphisme canonique (dit "de généralisation") π_1 P_{D''*} → π_1 P_{D'*}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Supports a precise formulation of the 'Teichmüller tower at infinity' as a stratified or exit-path diagram of (profinite) groups, of the kind used in anabelian work on the boundary of M̄_{g,n} (Hoshi–Mochizuki, Boggi). Mostly a historical priority point.

deep.surprise_reason: The page introduces a careful, general formalism (multinormal principal bundles, canonical generalisation maps between tube groups of strata, compatibility squares) that anticipates tangential base points and exit-path functoriality for M̄_{g,ν}. The mathematics is now standard in spirit, and this page itself contains only definitions and a trivial composite.
transcription_corrections: (233) should read π_1 P_{D''*} → π_1 P_{D'} (source D''*, not D'*).
The 'morphisme évident' should be P_{D''} → P_{D'}; the reading P_{D'} → P_{D''} is either a slip in the manuscript or a misreading.
In (231) the subscript on the target is 'Π_1 P_{D'*}' with an explicit index 1 in the image; the first Π lacks a visible '1' but means π_1.
Struck-out top-right annotation is roughly '(= D_2'^* des ... de ∂D'^*)'; it is deleted and illegible beyond that.
The struck line reads approximately 'compatibilité avec les opérations de [?] principales' / 'principales propriétés'; it is deleted.
